'''BID/60''', also called '''Singlet''',<ref name="Schmeh2008">{{cite book|author=Klaus Schmeh|title=Codeknacker gegen Codemacher: die faszinierende Geschichte der Verschlüsselung; &#91;Sachbuch&#93;|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cz9Fclgref4C&pg=PA116|year=2008|publisher=W3l GmbH|isbn=978-3-937137-89-6|pages=116–}}</ref> was a British [[encryption]] machine. It was used by the British intelligence services from around 1949 or 1950 onwards. The system is a [[rotor machine]], and would appear to have used 10 rotors. There are some apparent similarities between this machine and the US / NATO [[KL-7]] device.

[[Image:Singlet-rotor-tube-front.jpg|thumbnail|320px|The rotor tube of a Singlet machine, with 10 windows and stepping levers (similar to those on a [[KL-7]], suggesting 10 rotors.]]
In 2005, a Singlet machine was exhibited in the ''Enigma and Friends'' display at the [[Bletchley Park museum]].
